ai.description: The Andaman cobra reaches 1.5 meters. It is dark brown to black with a pale, indistinct hood mark. This species is distinguished by its slender build and lack of a distinct, high-contrast spectacle pattern.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Andaman Cobra (*Naja sagittifera*) is uniquely distinguished by the distinct, arrow-shaped mark on its hood, which differs from the spectacle or monocle patterns of mainland species.
ai.habitat: The Andaman Cobra inhabits the tropical evergreen and moist deciduous forests of the Andaman Islands, typically found in dense vegetation from sea level to low elevations.
ai.behavior: The Andaman Cobra is primarily diurnal, often seen actively foraging for small mammals and reptiles during the daylight hours rather than being strictly nocturnal.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Andaman Cobra is oviparous, laying clutches of 10–16 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon period, with hatchlings typically appearing by late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Andaman Cobra (*Naja sagittifera*) is endemic to the Andaman Islands in the Bay of Bengal, occurring from sea level up to moderate elevations within the archipelago.
